ref: Co-ordinates of the midpoint of a segment SolvedEx.1
stem: If A(3, 5), B(7, 9) and point Q divides seg AB in the ratio 2 : 3 then find co-ordinates of point Q.
solution:
In the given example let \((x_1, y_1) = (3, 5)\) and \((x_2, y_2) = (7, 9)\).

\(m : n = 2 : 3\)

According to section formula,

\(x = \dfrac{mx_2 + nx_1}{m + n} = \dfrac{2 \times 7 + 3 \times 3}{2 + 3} = \dfrac{23}{5}\)

\(y = \dfrac{my_2 + ny_1}{m + n} = \dfrac{2 \times 9 + 3 \times 5}{2 + 3} = \dfrac{33}{5}\)

\(\therefore\) Co-ordinates of Q are \(\left(\dfrac{23}{5}, \dfrac{33}{5}\right)\).

ref: Co-ordinates of the midpoint of a segment SolvedEx.2
stem: Find the co-ordinates of point P if P is the midpoint of a line segment AB with A(\(-4\), 2) and B(6, 2).
solution:
In the given example, suppose \((-4, 2) = (x_1, y_1)\) ; \((6, 2) = (x_2, y_2)\) and co-ordinates of P are \((x, y)\)

\(\therefore\) according to midpoint theorem,

\(x = \dfrac{x_1 + x_2}{2} = \dfrac{-4 + 6}{2} = \dfrac{2}{2} = 1\)

\(y = \dfrac{y_1 + y_2}{2} = \dfrac{2 + 2}{2} = \dfrac{4}{2} = 2\)

\(\therefore\) co-ordinates of midpoint P are (1, 2).
